363.35: in Greek mythology, satyrs are masculine, bestial spirits of woods and
hills.
 364.5: Gaius Julius Caesar Octavianus (63 B.C.-A.D. 14), first Roman emperor.
 364.11ff.: given the allusion to The Tragical History of Dr. Faustus (16o4) by the
English playwright Christopher Marlowe (1564-93)- "Was this the face that
launched a thousand ships I And burnt the topless towers of Ilium?" (V.i.94-
95) - this stanza presumably describes Helen of Troy, whose abduction by
Paris led to the Trojan War and the destruction of Troy.
 364.21-26: one of the paintings on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel by Mi-
chelangelo Buonarroti ( 14 75-1564) depicts God about to touch into life Adam,
the first man in the Bible.
 365.7: hysteria, causing suffocation or choking.
 365.13: in The Nature of Existeru:e (1921), the philosopher J. M. E. McTaggart
(1866-1925) argues that "all substances are compound."
 366.2: the Virgin Mary, mother of Christ in the Christian religion.
